title: Rainforest processes and the Peruvian Amazon

lines: **Biotic:** organisms. **Abiotic:** climate, light, water and soil. A change in one affects the others.
Heat and rain support growth, while vegetation changes habitats, water movement and soil protection.
**Nutrients:** biomass → litter → soil → root uptake. Warm, moist conditions speed decay.
**Water:** interception and transpiration help recycle moisture. Drip tips shed rain and buttress roots support trees.
**East of the Andes:** biodiversity, carbon storage, water regulation and Indigenous livelihoods.
Timber, food, tourism and mineral or energy resources also have economic value.
**Clearance:** habitat and biomass loss expose soil to leaching and erosion, while reducing water recycling.
Farming, logging, mining and access routes can reinforce one another’s impacts.
**Camisea:** energy and revenue alongside environmental and community concerns. Operating since 2004.
**Manu and Purús–Manu:** protected and connected habitats complement community management.
**Secure land rights, enforcement and sustainable income:** make conservation practical.
Evaluate who gains and whether forest functions remain. Protection on paper alone is insufficient.
**Warm-water reefs:** generally clear, sunlit tropical seas. Light supports photosynthetic partners.
Major examples include Andros, Florida, Mesoamerica, Red Sea, New Caledonia and Great Barrier reefs.
**Coral animals:** shelter algae and supply nutrients. **Algae:** photosynthesise and pass food to coral.
Nutrients circulate through organisms, waste and decomposition. Corals also capture food.
**The Bahamas:** the barrier reef, seagrass and mangroves provide feeding and nursery habitats.
Fish populations, coastal protection, fishing and tourism connect ecology to livelihoods.
**Heat stress:** bleaching may recover, but prolonged stress can kill coral.
Pollution, sediment, anchors, fishing pressure and habitat loss weaken the ecosystem.
**North and South Marine Parks:** reef-related protection. **West Side:** mangrove creeks and tidal flats.
**Crab Replenishment Reserve:** land-crab habitat and stocks. These protect different parts of Andros.
**Rules and monitoring:** need enforcement, cooperation and protection beyond boundaries.
Local action improves resilience. It cannot stop global warming on its own.
